text:
alex: Heads-up — we’re flipping the stricter fn-call validator in canary at 15:00 PT. quick decision: do we treat validator rejects as customer-facing errors that count toward quota/billing?

maria: Uh, if we count them customers will get surprised. a lot of apps currently rely on permissive tool invocations. :grimacing:

jamal: FWIW our offline run over last week shows ~0.9% of calls would be rejected by the stricter rules. distribution is heavy on one vendor adapter.

s_kapoor: My preference: metric-only for initial rollout (don’t increment tenant error_count), and surface a telemetry flag + sampled payloads so SRE/product can triage. Then switch to counting after a few weeks if false positives low.

alex: Agreed on metric-only default. but enterprise customers might want strict-enforced mode asap. need a per-org toggle.

maria: Per-org toggle is fine but that implies routing policy changes — we need to ensure router honors org-level enforcement setting before dispatch.

jamal: Router change is small: look up org.policy.strict_fnvalidate before dispatch; default false for existing orgs in canary. canary flag -> true for 5 orgs.

emily: Dashboard ask: show rejects as a separate series (validator.rejects) and top offending fields/adapter versions. engineers want quick link to sampled payloads (redact PII).

alex: On payload sampling: we should redact user text and only capture structural keys + adapter response. propose 1/1000 sample in canary and 1/100 for enterprise customers who opt-in.

jamal: example log line we’ll emit (sanitized):

```
validator.reject v=2 org=org-123 adapter=gizmo field=tool_args.missing token_bucket=1.2
```

s_kapoor: Metrics we need from the get-go:
- counter: validator.rejects.v2
- gauge: validator.rejects.percent_window (1h)
- tagged: validator.rejects.adapter, validator.rejects.field

maria: Also add: a hist for latency impact, validators.added_latency_ms because perf regressions kill adoption.

alex: Agreed. Regarding billing/quota: plan is metric-only for canary stage. After 3 weeks of low false-positive rate AND <0.1% tail errors, we’ll enable optional org toggle to count rejects. When org flips it on we increment error counters and those count toward rate limits.

emily: UX for Console: add a per-org banner if strict mode enabled: "Strict fn-call validation enforced — some calls rejected. Click to view examples (sampled)." Also a one-click rollback button for SEs.

maria: What about sampling privacy review? security needs to sign off on redact rules. @s_kapoor can you loop in security?

s_kapoor: Yep — I’ll open a ticket. default redact rules: remove any string values longer than 64 chars, hash short strings, strip emails/creditcard-like tokens.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: version=fn-validate-v2 target=canary-5pct ts=2351112400

jamal: quick test idea: add synthetic repo that intentionally emits borderline shapes to measure false accepts/rejects. run daily against canary.

alex: Good. Action items:
- jamal: router check + per-org toggle (PR today)
- emily: dashboard tiles + console banner mockups
- s_kapoor: security ticket for sampling/redaction rules
- maria: contract a small set of enterprise orgs for opt-in strict testing
- jamal/maria: synthetic tests and daily run config

maria: I’ll shepherd the customer comms draft once we have numbers.

alex: Thanks. If we see >0.2% unexpected rejects in first 24h we pause rollout. keep pings in #eng-oncall and drop snapshots in the canary channel. :thumbsup:

emily: noted — I’ll add dashboard alerts (pager threshold = 0.2% per 24h by org).

alex: closing loop — will check back after 6h.
